title: Is Insulin Growth Factor-Like Family Member 2 (IGFL2) a possible early marker molecule for a successful response to biologic therapy in psoriasis?
summary: Modern drugs from the group of biologics intervene in the inflammatory process by specifically blocking the signalling cascades and allow severe psoriasis to heal quickly where conventional treatments have often failed. However, each patient responds differently well and quickly to the respective preparation, so that the clinical success of the therapy can often only be evaluated after several months (3-6 months) of therapy. Therefore, it would be important to characterise marker genes that can provide information about a response to biologics therapy shortly after the start of therapy.

interventions.name: 15 psoriasis patients treated with a biologic

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All adult, male and female patients can participate in this study, 
- who have severe to moderate psoriasis for which guideline-recommended therapy with one of the following already approved biologics (secukinumab, brodalumab, ixekizumab) is recommended.
- who understand the nature, significance and scope of the study
- who are able to understand and follow the instructions of the study staff
- who have signed an informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
- Minority
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding
- lack of informed consent
- are incapable of giving consent and / or are unable to understand the nature, significance and scope of the study and to give their consent in writing.
